Pertanyaan Live

Kirim Pertanyaan

Scan kode QR ini untuk membuka halaman pertanyaan. Cocok ditampilkan di OBS atau proyektor saat sesi live.

""" end defp shimmer_classes(%{value: 1, classes: classes}) do cond do Enum.any?(classes, &String.starts_with?(&1, "qr-frame")) -> ["qrf-shimmer-dot", "qrf-shimmer-finder"] Enum.any?(classes, &String.starts_with?(&1, "qr-inner-frame")) -> ["qrf-shimmer-dot", "qrf-shimmer-inner"] true -> ["qrf-shimmer-dot", "qrf-shimmer-data"] end end defp shimmer_classes(_), do: ["qrf-shimmer-dot", "qrf-shimmer-off"] defp shimmer_style(%{value: 1, element_index: idx}) when is_integer(idx) do delay = rem(idx * 37, 240) / 100 "animation-delay: #{delay}s;" end defp shimmer_style(_), do: "" defp display_url(url) do url |> String.replace_prefix("https://", "") |> String.replace_prefix("http://", "") end end

defmodule DonatexWeb.QrFeedbackLiveTest do
  use DonatexWeb.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest

  alias Donatex.Qr

  @questions_url "https://feedback.rizafahmi.com/questions"

  describe "GET /qr-feedback" do
    test "renders feedback QR slide with questions URL", %{conn: conn} do
      {:ok, view, html} = live(conn, ~p"/qr-feedback")

      assert html =~ "Kirim"
      assert html =~ "Pertanyaan"
      assert html =~ "feedback.rizafahmi.com/questions"
      assert html =~ "Download PNG"
      assert html =~ "Download SVG"
      assert has_element?(view, "#qrf-code .qrf-svg-base svg")
      assert has_element?(view, ".qrf-shimmer-grid")
    end

    test "obs mode hides export panel", %{conn: conn} do
      {:ok, _view, html} = live(conn, ~p"/qr-feedback?obs=1")

      refute html =~ "Download PNG"
      assert html =~ "Scan untuk kirim pertanyaan"
    end

    test "download png triggers push event", %{conn: conn} do
      {:ok, view, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/qr-feedback")

      view |> element("#qrfDownloadPng") |> render_click()
      assert_push_event(view, "qrf:download_png", %{filename: "qr-questions.png"})
    end

    test "download svg triggers push event", %{conn: conn} do
      {:ok, view, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/qr-feedback")

      view |> element("#qrfDownloadSvg") |> render_click()
      assert_push_event(view, "qrf:download_svg", %{filename: "qr-questions.svg"})
    end

    test "sets noindex robots metadata", %{conn: conn} do
      {:ok, _view, html} = live(conn, ~p"/qr-feedback")

      assert html =~ ~s(<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow")
    end
  end

  describe "Qr.questions_url/0" do
    test "points at the questions page" do
      assert Qr.questions_url() == @questions_url
    end
  end
end

Here's what I built — a fresh `/qr-feedback` page (not based on `/qr`) that matches the doom-emacs vibe of `/`.

## Live page

**`/qr-feedback`** — broadcast slide for your audience:
- Same card aesthetic as `/`: rounded panels, accent glows, doom palette (`#9ccfd8`, `#c4a7e7`, `#f6c177`, `#eb6f92`, `#1f1d2e`)
- Animated QR: orbiting gradient halo, terminal-style corner brackets, scan line, twinkling data modules
- Encodes **`https://feedback.rizafahmi.com/questions`**
- **Download PNG** and **Download SVG** buttons
- **Copy URL** button

**OBS mode** (minimal chrome, QR-focused):

`/qr-feedback?obs=1`

## Static exports

Generated in `.scratch/qr-export/`:

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `qr-questions.svg` | White background, scannable |
| `qr-questions.png` | Same, rasterized |
| `qr-questions-branded.svg` | Doom dark bg (`#1f1d2e`) + light modules |
| `qr-questions-branded.png` | Branded raster |

## How to use on stream

1. **Browser source in OBS** → open `/qr-feedback?obs=1`
2. **Static slide** → use PNG/SVG from `.scratch/qr-export/` or download from the page
3. **Full slide with instructions** → use `/qr-feedback` (non-OBS mode)

Run `mix phx.server` and visit [http://localhost:4000/qr-feedback](http://localhost:4000/qr-feedback) to preview.

The design is intentionally different from `/qr`: no minimize/expand pill, no lightning-bolt overlay — instead a donate-page-style broadcast card with terminal corners and a shimmer grid. Want a branded PNG with the full card frame (not just the QR), or tweaks to copy/animation speed?

Pulling the app’s exact palette so I can give you QRCode Monkey settings that match.

Use these on [QRCode Monkey](https://www.qrcode-monkey.com/) so it matches the app’s doom / console vibe.

## Content
- **Type:** URL  
- **URL:** `https://feedback.rizafahmi.com/questions`

## Recommended (best scan on stream)

High contrast, still on-brand.

### Set Colors
| Field | Value |
|--------|--------|
| **Foreground** | Single Color → `#1f1d2e` |
| **Color Gradient** | Off (or use the gradient recipe below) |
| **Custom Eye Color** | On |
| **Eye Color (outer)** | `#9ccfd8` (cyan accent) |
| **Eye Color (inner)** | `#c4a7e7` (purple accent) |
| **Background Color** | `#ffffff` |

### Customize Design
| Field | Pick |
|--------|------|
| **Body Shape** | Rounded / smooth squares (not too thin) |
| **Eye Frame Shape** | Rounded square / leaf-ish frame |
| **Eye Ball Shape** | Circle or rounded diamond |
| **Logo** | Optional — only if small; keep error correction high |

### Export
- Resolution: max / high quality  
- Format: **PNG** for OBS, **SVG** for print/slides  
- Scan-test before going live

---

## Gradient option (more “Notable” feel)

Same as above, but:

| Field | Value |
|--------|--------|
| **Color Gradient** | On → **Linear** |
| **Gradient color 1** | `#1f1d2e` |
| **Gradient color 2** | `#2a4550` (or soft cyan-slate) |
| **Eyes** | Outer `#9ccfd8`, Inner `#c4a7e7` |
| **Background** | `#ffffff` |

Keep the body mostly dark so phones still read it.

---

## Branded dark look (matches site, weaker scan)

Only if you want it on a dark slide and will test scanners:

| Field | Value |
|--------|--------|
| **Foreground** | `#e0def4` |
| **Eye outer** | `#9ccfd8` |
| **Eye inner** | `#f6c177` |
| **Background** | `#1f1d2e` |

Monkey prefers dark-on-light; if scans fail, switch back to the white-background recipe.

---

## App palette cheat sheet

| Role | Hex |
|------|-----|
| Deep slate / modules | `#1f1d2e` |
| Cyan accent | `#9ccfd8` |
| Purple accent | `#c4a7e7` |
| Gold accent | `#f6c177` |
| Rose accent | `#eb6f92` |
| Soft text | `#e0def4` |
| White quiet zone | `#ffffff` |

**Rule of thumb:** dark body + cyan/purple eyes + white quiet zone = doom-emacs vibe and reliable scans.
